prompt: A male lion's full head fills the frame, the thick mane of dark brown and amber radiating from the crown to below the jaw, every strand distinct and individually lit. The wide-set amber eyes are calm and forward-facing, the broad nose is smooth and pink-brown, and the mouth is closed in a relaxed expression. The whisker pads are full and round, and the short tawny fur across the cheeks transitions into the dense, coarse mane at the jawline. The light is warm and even, and no background is visible—only the lion's head, mane, and the space between the strands.

A Bengal tiger's full head fills the frame, the orange-and-black striped face perfectly symmetrical, the white ruff beneath the jaw thick and full. The pale green eyes are steady and direct, the black nose is broad and damp, and the long white whiskers fan outward from the muzzle pads. Every stripe is sharp, the short velvet fur between the stripes catches the light, and the rounded ears show their white ocelli spots on the dark backs. No background is visible—only the tiger's face and the dense fur of the ruff.

A snowy owl's full head fills the frame, the perfectly round white face and bright yellow eyes dominating the image. The dark barring on the crown feathers, the small hooked beak half-hidden in the facial disc, and the fine feather filaments around the eyes are all uniformly sharp. The ear tufts are absent, the head smooth and domed, and the feathers grade from pure white at the throat to faintly barred grey at the crown. No background is visible—only the owl's immaculate white plumage and the piercing yellow irises.

A silverback gorilla's full head fills the frame, the broad black face and the pronounced sagittal crest sharp and detailed. The deep-set brown eyes are thoughtful and calm, the wide nostrils flare gently, and the lips are closed over the heavy jaw. The skin of the face is smooth and dark, and the coarse black hair frames the face from the brow to the cheeks, with silver-grey hairs visible at the temples. No background is visible—only the gorilla's face, the texture of the skin, and the wiry hair.

A bald eagle's full head fills the frame, the snow-white feathers of the crown and nape immaculate against the golden-yellow hooked beak and the pale, fierce eye. Every feather on the head is individually defined, the beak's waxy cere and the nostril are in sharp detail, and the eye's dark pupil is ringed with a pale straw-coloured iris. The white feathers grade to dark brown at the neck's base, and the beak's curved tip shows a faint scratch of wear. No background is visible—only the eagle's white head, yellow beak, and the sharp intensity of the eye.

A grey wolf's full head fills the frame, the grizzled fur of grey, cream, and black tapering to a narrow muzzle and a dark wet nose. The golden-amber eyes are locked forward, the ears are erect and edged in dark fur, and the thick winter ruff around the neck creates a dense collar of layered guard hairs. The whiskers are long and pale, and the mouth is closed, the lips dark against the lighter muzzle fur. No background is visible—only the wolf's head, the texture of the layered pelt, and the quiet alertness of the expression.

A red fox's full head fills the frame, the sharp triangular face of vivid orange fur tapering to a black nose and a white chin. The amber eyes are bright and inquisitive, the oversized ears are erect and black-backed, and the cheek ruffs are thick with pale cream fur. Every guard hair, every whisker, and the faint dark tear-lines running from the inner eyes to the muzzle are uniformly sharp. No background is visible—only the fox's compact, alert face and the rich orange coat.

A snow leopard's full head fills the frame, the pale grey fur patterned with dark rosettes across the cheeks and forehead, the thick smoke-coloured ruffs framing the face. The eyes are a clear pale green, the broad nose is pink and grey, and the long whiskers are white and stiff. The fur is dense and plush, the ears small and rounded with dark backs, and the overall expression is serene and unhurried. No background is visible—only the leopard's extraordinary patterned face and the luxurious depth of the winter coat.

A polar bear's full head fills the frame, the broad cream-white face showing the small dark eyes, the large black nose, and the powerful jaw. The fur is dense and slightly yellowish at the muzzle, each hair visible as a hollow translucent tube catching the light. The small rounded ears sit low on the wide skull, and the lips are dark against the pale fur. The head is massive and blunt, and the expression is calm, the dark eyes steady. No background is visible—only the bear's heavy white head and the coarse, light-catching texture of the Arctic coat.

An African elephant's full head fills the frame, the enormous grey ears fanned slightly outward, the trunk curled loosely beneath the chin, and the deep wrinkles and folds of the skin mapping every decade of its life. The small amber eye sits in a web of creased skin, and the base of a single ivory tusk emerges from the upper lip. The skin texture is extraordinary—cracked, ridged, and dusted with dry earth in the creases. No background is visible—only the elephant's monumental head, the papery ears, and the ancient, textured hide.

A great horned owl's full head fills the frame, the prominent ear tufts erect, the enormous yellow-orange eyes staring directly forward, and the facial disc of concentric brown-and-cream feather rings framing the dark hooked beak. The feather detail is razor-sharp, from the fine barbs of the ear tufts to the soft down around the beak and the mottled brown-and-white barring on the throat. The eyes are the dominant feature—enormous, unblinking, each iris a ring of deep gold around the black pupil. No background is visible—only the owl's fierce, symmetrical face.

A mandrill's full head fills the frame, the extraordinary face a vivid palette of electric blue nose ridges, scarlet nostrils and lips, and a golden-orange beard. The close-set amber eyes are framed by the blue ridges, and the fur of the forehead is olive-grey, grading to the beard's bright fan of coarse hair. Every ridge, every pore in the coloured skin, and every wiry hair in the beard is uniformly sharp. No background is visible—only the mandrill's chromatic face, the most colourful of any mammal, rendered in full unflinching detail.

A green sea turtle's full head fills the frame, the smooth mosaic of olive-and-brown scales covering the skull, the large dark eye gentle and ancient, and the beak-like mouth closed in a slight downward curve. The scute pattern on the head is a jigsaw of individual plates, each outlined in a faintly lighter edge, and the skin around the eye is thin enough to show the orbital bone beneath. No background is visible—only the turtle's calm, prehistoric face and the smooth geometry of its scaled skin.

A harpy eagle's full head fills the frame, the raised crest of dark grey feathers fanning behind the pale face, the massive hooked beak slate-grey, and the piercing grey eyes rimmed with dark lashes. The facial disc is subtle—pale grey feathers radiating outward—and the crest feathers are individually sharp, each one a long, broad plume. The expression is imperious, the beak enormous relative to the head, and the nostrils are exposed ovals at the beak's base. No background is visible—only the eagle's extraordinary crested head and the powerful architecture of the beak.

A jaguar's full head fills the frame, the broad golden face covered in tight rosettes—each one a ring of dark spots surrounding a lighter centre. The eyes are green-gold and half-lidded, the broad nose is pink and dark-spotted, and the jaw is massive and squared. The whisker pads are prominent and the short white whiskers fan outward, and the ears are small and rounded with a dark spot on each back. No background is visible—only the jaguar's powerful, patterned face and the short, dense coat.

A resplendent quetzal's full head fills the frame, the iridescent emerald-green feathers of the crown and nape shifting between green and gold with each barb's angle. The short yellow beak is partly hidden in the fluffy green breast feathers, and the dark eye is large and round. The feathers of the crest are hair-like and wispy, standing upright in a shaggy crown, and the throat transitions from green to vivid crimson at the base of the frame. No background is visible—only the quetzal's jewel-like head and the metallic, light-shifting plumage.

A Komodo dragon's full head fills the frame, the heavy, armoured face covered in pebbly scales of dark grey-brown, the forked yellow tongue partially extended from the closed mouth. The beady dark eyes are small and set far back on the wide skull, and the nostrils are rounded openings on the squared-off snout. The individual scales vary in size—large and flat on the jaw, small and granular around the eyes—and the loose skin beneath the throat hangs in a heavy dewlap. No background is visible—only the dragon's primeval, reptilian head and the textured mosaic of scales.

An Arctic fox's full head fills the frame in its winter coat, the face a dense sphere of pure white fur, the small dark eyes and black nose the only points of contrast. The fur is incredibly thick—the ears are barely visible, buried in the plush coat—and every hair catches the light, creating a soft luminosity across the entire face. The whiskers are white and nearly invisible against the fur, and the expression is bright and alert despite the minimal features. No background is visible—only the fox's white face, a study in monochrome broken only by the dark punctuation of the eyes and nose.

A peregrine falcon's full head fills the frame, the dark helmet-like cap of slate-grey feathers covering the crown and framing the face in a sharp moustachial stripe of black. The large dark eye is surrounded by a bare yellow orbital ring, and the hooked beak is blue-grey with a dark tip and a yellow cere at the base. The throat is white, and the transition from the dark cap to the pale feathers is abrupt and clean. No background is visible—only the falcon's compact, aerodynamic head and the precision of its predator's markings.

A humpback whale's full head fills the frame as it surfaces, the dark grey skin barnacle-encrusted, the knobbed tubercles along the rostrum each sprouting a single sensory hair. The blowhole is a pair of slits at the crown, and one eye is visible—small, dark, and deeply set in a fold of skin. The ventral grooves of the throat are faintly visible below the jaw, and the baleen plates inside the slightly open mouth show as a curtain of dark bristles. No background is visible—only the whale's immense, barnacled head and the glistening wet skin catching the light in broad, wet highlights.
